scope: R2-08 fixed timer deadline and R2-10 existing wrapper caller; source/documentation only; no service invocation or approval
documentationFacts: OnActiveSec uses activation time, OnBootSec uses boot time, and OnStartupSec uses manager startup. The last two differ for a user manager. A past boot/startup timer fires immediately. Monotonic timers normally pause during suspend; WakeSystem changes the clock choice.
AccuracySec admits a window after the target; configure and validate at most one second under the normative contract, with no extra random delay.
The timer target Unit and NextElapseUSecMonotonic are independent facts. The latter is a microsecond CLOCK_MONOTONIC timestamp; neither may be inferred from active status alone.
reviewInferences: A boot-anchored monotonic timer can avoid the measured relative-activation extension if the actual user-manager clock identity and installed semantics match. Verify actual target and elapse against authenticated outer start before resource start. This is an implementation option, not live validation.
RuntimeMaxSec alone remains activation-relative; a separate authenticated absolute bootstrap bound is still required. Timer correctness cannot establish the separate +1606 bound.

The existing static wrapper validates control and execv of supplied argv. Its source must remain present; validate the entire reviewed proof-server command at the parent before startup. Do not add an unreviewed self-certified config record or infer full argv from a two-element prefix.
expectedCases: Activation delay leaves the same target, including fractional second rounding toward the conservative bound.
Reject missing/zero/non-numeric/too-late next elapse, wrong Unit, unexpected clock basis, excessive accuracy/random delay, stale boot/time namespace and setup expiration.
Repeated cleanup commands and writes share one absolute budget; remaining <=0 starts no new operation.
Changed proof-server argv/config denies before resource start while the pinned static wrapper parser/deadline/descendant behavior remains covered.
limitations: No real user-manager timer was created or queried. No Docker/container read or start occurred. Documentation does not establish actual namespace/reachability/activation behavior.
